A01_broken_access_control.checked: TelegramSender returns uniform 404 (code:null, message:'Bot not found') for both bot-not-found and status!=CONNECTED via .filter(status==CONNECTED).switchIfEmpty(AppException.notFound(MESSAGE_BOT_NOT_FOUND)) at TelegramSender.java:113-115 — matches Decision 7 and the BotService.requireConnectedBot precedent. BotService.sendTestMessage calls requireConnectedBot FIRST (line 119) BEFORE branching on bot.getOwnerChatId() (line 124), so a foreign or disconnected bot collapses to 404 before the ownerChatId check is ever reachable. SecurityConfig.java has zero diff vs pre-feature (git-confirmed); the existing /api/** authenticated rule (line 71) continues to cover POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/bot/test-message — verified by BotControllerIT.postTestMessage_in07_seededOwnerChatId_returns200_emitsEvent (positive auth path) and an unauthenticated case asserting 401 at line 968-971. BotResponse does NOT surface the new internal ownerChatId field — record components verified at BotResponse.java:9-16 (only telegramBotId/telegramUsername/telegramFirstName/tokenSuffix/status/connectedAt). No new endpoints; no cross-tenant leakage path introduced.

A02_cryptographic_failures.checked: Per-call decrypt enforced; no caching: TelegramSender.sendOnce decodes Base64 IV + ciphertext and calls tokenEncryptor.decrypt(iv, ct) on every invocation (TelegramSender.java:140-150). The plaintext token is captured ONLY in the Mono closure (local variable `token` at line 150), never assigned to a field, never logged, never serialized, never pushed to a background scheduler — comment block at TelegramSender.java:41-44 documents the invariant. requireValidTokenShape(token) is invoked IMMEDIATELY after decrypt (line 153) and BEFORE webClient URI construction (line 165-166) — ordering non-negotiable per Architecture step 4 and verified by test sendText_malformedTokenInBot_throwsBotTokenInvalidException_beforeHttp (request count==0). Decrypt error contract honored verbatim: the try/catch at TelegramSender.java:140-146 is SCOPED to Base64.getDecoder().decode(...) only and catches solely IllegalArgumentException, mapping to BotTokenInvalidException(botId, 'decryption failed'). The subsequent tokenEncryptor.decrypt(iv, ct) call at line 150 sits DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE the catch (explicit comment at lines 147-149 invokes Risk R7), so an IllegalStateException from TokenEncryptor.decrypt (AEADBadTagException-wrapped tamper OR misconfigured bean) propagates to GlobalErrorHandler.handleThrowable (common/GlobalErrorHandler.java:43-48 — generic 500 'Internal server error' body, no stacktrace leak). The pass-through unit test sendText_decryptThrowsIllegalState_propagatesAsInternalError_notBotTokenInvalid (TelegramSenderTest.java:552-576) stubs TokenEncryptor to throw IllegalStateException and asserts .isInstanceOf(IllegalStateException.class).isNotInstanceOf(BotTokenInvalidException.class) — exact behavior the contract demands. Risk R7 confirmed as accepted limitation (no contradiction). BotTokenLeakTest holds: (a) BotResponse record components do not include encryptedTokenCiphertext/encryptedTokenIv/token/webhookSecretHash (BotTokenLeakTest.java:19-49); (b) Bot.java declares NO toString override (Bot.java has no toString method; encrypted-token fields are also @JsonIgnore at line 54-61, preventing Jackson serialization). Exception messages do NOT embed plaintext tokens — BotTokenInvalidException carries only botId + a hard-coded reason string ('decryption failed' or 'invalid token shape after decrypt' or 'Token is invalid or revoked'); TelegramSendException's scrubbedDescription parameter contract (TelegramSendException.java:11-12) explicitly documents the caller's pre-scrub obligation, and every TelegramSender call site that constructs TelegramSendException passes either a fixed sentinel ('timeout', 'transient_failure_exhausted') or `scrubbed` from TelegramApiClient.scrubTokens(...) — verified at TelegramSender.java:119, 203, 217, 237.

A03_injection.checked: parse_mode defaults to null in the entire call chain: BotService.sendTestMessage passes `null` to TelegramSender.sendText (BotService.java:129-130), and TelegramSender.sendOnce only adds 'parse_mode' to the request body when the argument is non-null (TelegramSender.java:161-163). Decision 6 defends Epic 06/07 future callers from HTML/Markdown injection in Telegram-rendered output. Tests pin both branches: sendText_parseModeNull_omitsFieldFromBody (TelegramSenderTest.java:201-215) and sendText_parseModeHtml_includesFieldInBody (line 217-229). URI built via WebClient placeholder pattern at TelegramSender.java:165-166: webClient.post().uri('/bot{token}/sendMessage', token) with DefaultUriBuilderFactory.EncodingMode.NONE set at constructor line 96 — mirrors TelegramApiClient. Token never concatenated into a raw URI string. Request body built via HashMap with explicit .put() calls (TelegramSender.java:158-163), no JSON-literal string concatenation. Confirmed no SQL or shell paths in this feature: only Mongo via BotRepository.findById (reactive driver, parameterised) and WebClient outbound HTTP.

A05_security_misconfiguration.checked: SecurityConfig.java has zero diff vs pre-feature state (git diff confirmed; the file is read-only for this feature). The /api/** authenticated rule (SecurityConfig.java:71) continues to cover the test-message endpoint. No new application.properties / application-test.properties keys introduced — the feature reuses existing app.telegram.base-url and app.bot.token-encryption-key. build.gradle untouched — okhttp3:mockwebserver:4.12.0 was already a testImplementation. No new @CrossOrigin or permitAll annotations. No new @ConditionalOnProperty toggles that could relax non-prod profile behavior. The CORS allowlist (SecurityConfig.java:97-107) still restricts origin to ${app.url} and only permits the X-XSRF-TOKEN custom header — unchanged. CSRF protection via CookieServerCsrfTokenRepository continues to apply to all state-changing requests including /test-message.

A07_identification_authentication.checked: Auth flow unchanged. The new endpoint POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/bot/test-message reuses the /api/** authenticated chain (SecurityConfig.java:71). BotController.testMessage (BotController.java:60-68) derives ownerId from currentUserId() (BotController.java:81-87) which extracts AppUserDetails.id() from ReactiveSecurityContextHolder — sourced from the authenticated session principal, NOT from any caller-controlled request-body field. The endpoint accepts no JSON body (only path variables + standard headers). projectId is path-variable scoped and validated by BotService.requireConnectedBot → projectService.requireOwned (BotService.java:142) — same ownership precondition as Get/Connect/Disconnect. No JWT/session/MFA semantics altered.

A09_logging_monitoring_failures.checked: Audit events written by sender on both terminal outcomes: telegram_message_sent on success (TelegramSender.java:120-125, owner-id-attributed via EventService.logEvent) and telegram_send_failed on terminal failure (TelegramSender.java:126-133). The isTerminalAuditable guard at line 256-262 ensures transient/429 internal exceptions consumed by retry loops do NOT spuriously emit a failure event — only BotTokenInvalidException and TelegramSendException are auditable. failedMetadata (line 272-287) carries attempts (always), errorCode (only when TelegramSendException, may be null), and errorDescription = TelegramSendException.getMessage() — which is the PRE-SCRUBBED description (TelegramSendException constructor explicitly documents 'callers MUST pre-scrub'); all TelegramSender call sites supply either a fixed internal sentinel ('timeout' at line 119, 'transient_failure_exhausted' at line 237) or a value already routed through TelegramApiClient.scrubTokens(...) (line 189 and line 215). All 7 required external-string log sites are scrubbed: map4xx WARN (line 202) — `scrubbed`; ok=false mapper WARN (line 216) — `scrubbed`; 5xx retry observer WARN (line 233-235) — `scrubTokens(rs.failure().getMessage())`; 429 announce WARN (line 199) — `scrubbed`; terminal-failure doOnError ERROR (line 128-129) — `scrubTokens(ex.getMessage())` (also handles the overall-timeout and transport-error terminal-emission paths since they re-route through the same doOnError). The 429 wait-announcement at line 247 emits ONLY internally computed delaySeconds and jitterMs numbers — no external string echoed, so no scrubber needed at that exact site (the prior mapper site at line 199 already scrubbed the description before raising TelegramRateLimitException). ListAppender unit tests cover each scrubber site: sendText_tokenIn4xxDescription_scrubbed_warnLevel (TelegramSenderTest.java:660-672), sendText_tokenIn5xxRetryLog_scrubbed_warnLevel (line 674-693), sendText_tokenIn429RetryLog_scrubbed_warnLevel (line 695-711), sendText_tokenInTerminalFailureLog_scrubbed_errorLevel (line 713-735), sendText_tokenInTransportErrorMessage_scrubbed (line 737-769). bot_test_message_sent (BotService.sendTestMessage line 134-136) is written only on success — Decision 3 enforced; no double-write on failure path.

findings.issue: Risk R7 (accepted): TelegramSender.java:147-150 deliberately lets IllegalStateException from TokenEncryptor.decrypt propagate as 500 because corrupted/tampered ciphertext (AEADBadTagException wrapped) and a misconfigured TokenEncryptor bean are indistinguishable at the call site. The implementation honors the documented mitigation verbatim — scoped catch on Base64.getDecoder().decode IllegalArgumentException only (line 143), decrypt outside the catch (line 150), pass-through verified by sendText_decryptThrowsIllegalState_propagatesAsInternalError_notBotTokenInvalid (TelegramSenderTest.java:552-576). GlobalErrorHandler.handleThrowable (common/GlobalErrorHandler.java:43-48) maps to a generic 500 'Internal server error' body with no stacktrace leak, surfacing the issue to ops monitoring rather than a user-facing 422.

Risk R11 (accepted): No per-endpoint rate limit on POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/bot/test-message. An authenticated owner can spam the endpoint up to Telegram's own per-bot ~30 msg/sec cap. The feature does not introduce new abuse vectors beyond the existing endpoint; abuse is bounded by Telegram's response and the requirement of an authenticated session for the bot's owner.

Risk R12 (accepted): chatId and messageId stored in events.metadata (telegram_message_sent, telegram_send_failed, bot_test_message_sent) are end-user PII (Telegram numeric ids). Long-term retention policy is not defined in this feature; the new event types reuse the same metadata shape as the existing bot_connected / bot_disconnected events, so 07-telegram-sender does not change the platform's PII surface.
